tool: vep-rs 0.4.0 (reports itself as Ensembl VEP (Rust) v116.2)
tool_source: github.com/natera-open-source/vep-rs, release v0.4.0 (2026-10-16), Apache-2.0; x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu tarball, SHA256 verified against SHA256SUMS
database: Perl VEP 115 GRCh38 offline cache, chr22 only, converted to JSON by scripts/data/storable_to_json.pl run inside docker://ensemblorg/ensembl-vep:release_116.2 (apptainer). 51/51 files, 12225 transcripts, 60 MB, 11 s
level: capability and cost probe; no level claimed
cache: gnomAD v4.1 GRCh38 joint AF>=1% blueprint, chr22 slices (the same cuts the SnpEff clinical gate used)
note: Not a direct-vs-cached comparison. Three questions, all answered: (1) a usable JSON cache can be converted from the Perl VEP 115 cache; (2) the converted cache reaches core consequences plus SYMBOL/BIOTYPE/CANONICAL/CCDS/TSL/ENSP/SWISSPROT/TREMBL/EXON/HGVSc/HGVSp, and nothing clinical -- storable_to_json.pl writes transcripts only, vep-rs logs 'No variations directory found', and 231 missense consequences carry no SIFT, PolyPhen, DOMAINS, AF, gnomAD or CLIN_SIG; (3) two-point fit at 16385 and 314314 records gives 5.68 us/variant (core) to 14.00 us/variant (--everything) with 0.16-0.25 s start-up. --everything additionally warns that --regulatory has no effect. See ANALYSIS.md.
